A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TriDi and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references and complete supplementary sections. Corresponding content can be reliably matched across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, benchmark comparisons, ablations, qualitative applications and a user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds quantitative evaluations of sampling modes, conditioning choices and text-template training.

M1.justification: The trilateral diffusion transformer, contact-text representation, guidance, augmentation, losses and optional hand refinement remain unchanged in Sections 4, 8 and 12. The added s-TriDi-HO model serves as an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions use BEHAVE, GRAB, InterCap and OMOMO, plus HPS scenes, DAMON reconstructions and unseen object geometries. The seven conditioning modes and text/contact inputs already appear in v1; v2 adds measurements and another text-query example within this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds s-TriDi-HO, trained specifically for H,O|I, as a comparator under contact-map and text conditioning in Table S4. Existing comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. CG-HOI is reported as a failed adaptation, without a scored comparison.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation with diversity, multimodality and contact-presence measurements, 200-sample subset calculations, and contact-map versus text comparisons. The user-study interface changes from one displayed view per sample to four orthogonal views (Figure 10 versus S3). Section 5.1 also changes the stated MPJPE unit from mm to cm; existing table values, training settings and dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a single-template versus full-template ablation and an unseen-wording example in Section 8. Table S4 extends the joint-versus-specialized training analysis to H,O|I and compares text with contact-map conditioning. The original augmentation, guidance and interaction-modality ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three sampling runs and mean/variance for distribution comparisons. Added tables continue reporting variability without introducing a new uncertainty-reporting practice, explicit replication increase, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables S3–S4 add all-mode diversity/contact results and H,O|I comparisons; the template ablation adds recall values of 63.5 versus 75.0. User-study preferences change from 82.0% to 87.75% against GNet and 80.8% to 90.25% against ObjPOP+cVAE; corresponding preferences over ground truth change from 50.3% to 47.75% and 43.0% to 56.25%. These use changed viewing conditions. Tables 1–2 and the original ablation tables retain their numerical entries.

T1.justification: Section 13 introduces mathematical definitions for the newly used diversity and object-category multimodality metrics in Equations 25–26. Existing diffusion equations, losses and refinement mathematics remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the seven-mode joint model, shared contact/text representation, up-to-47% comparison claim and applications. The introduction clarifies dataset annotation as adding objects to human-contact data, an application already stated in v1's abstract.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning weaker text conditioning, recall's importance for sparse contact maps, and a hypothesized explanation for CG-HOI's failed static adaptation. It qualifies best-of-three errors as approximating upper-bound performance and replaces the anti-memorization interpretation with nontrivial generation. Existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 attributes contact-map thresholding to BEHAVE and specifies 200-sample subsets for the new metrics. It removes the explicit 3-NN implementation statement for the retained retrieval baseline. Core implementation parameters, hardware, timing, project-page information and code-release promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Action2Motion as the source of diversity/multimodality evaluation and expands its positioning relative to CG-HOI through the static-adaptation discussion. The remaining cited works and related-work narrative are retained.

P1.justification: Experimental descriptions receive localized rewrites and clarifications, Section 9 becomes 'Additional Evaluation,' and the appendix gains explanatory paragraphs. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables S3–S4, expands the contact-map figure with another prompt, replaces the user-study screenshot and relocates the template listing. Supplementary figures and tables receive S-prefixed numbering and reflow; most existing displays remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1's numerical evaluation concentrates on two modes; v2 strengthens support for the broader claims through all-mode checks, template ablation and conditioning comparisons. Four-view user-study presentation also enables fuller visual assessment. These provide useful additional validation, although diversity/contact-presence checks offer limited evidence of realism and the revised preference percentages require interpretation under changed viewing conditions.
